content.text:
Mechanically yes — but checking it moved my ranking, because option 2 doesn't actually achieve what I claimed.

## The generic part does apply cleanly

A `readLiveTranscript` / `ReadTranscriptForStorage` helper is agent-agnostic, and `SanitizeTranscriptForStorage` is a **no-op for all 8 non-Codex agents** — none implements `TranscriptSanitizer`. So the refactor is behavior-preserving for Claude Code, Gemini, OpenCode, Cursor, Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi, and Vogon, and only changes Codex.

Worth saying explicitly: **there's no hidden drift for the other agents today.** Redaction, image externalization, and chunking all rewrite or split *within* line boundaries, so raw line/message counts equal stored ones everywhere except Codex.

## But it wouldn't give you one coordinate system

I described option 2 as "Entire never holds raw bytes, so there's only one basis." That's wrong, because a whole family of capabilities reads the raw file **by path**, straight off disk, bypassing any byte-level boundary:

| Capability | Called at |
|---|---|
| `GetTranscriptPosition(path)` — *this is raw-basis consumer #2* | `hooks.go:1888, 2719`, `state.go:123` |
| `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(path, offset)` | `hooks.go:1969`, `lifecycle.go:820, 1136` |
| `ExtractPrompts(path, offset)` | `lifecycle.go:784`, `attach_transcript.go:68`, `rewind.go:855` |

To make those agree you'd have to either convert them to byte-based signatures or point them at a sanitized file. And they're implemented by **9 things — the 8 built-ins plus `external.Agent`**, which forwards them over the external-agent protocol (`external/external.go:300`, `external/capabilities.go:96`).

So converting the signatures is a **wire-format change for third-party agents.**

The "point them at a sanitized file" variant looks tempting because Entire already materializes one — `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` has been sanitized since commit 1. But it's only refreshed at Stop, and `GetTranscriptPosition` is consulted *mid-turn*, so it'd be stale exactly when needed. Fixing that means rewriting a multi-MB file more often on a hot path — trading the problem for the one we just fixed.

## What that does to the ranking

Option 2's cost scales with agent count and reaches the external protocol, while its benefit here is Codex-only. That's a bad trade for a display-scoping bug in one agent, so I'd demote it as *the fix for this*.

**Option 1 (blank instead of drop) now looks clearly best**: it makes both bases coincide without touching a single agent interface, needs no migration, and retroactively corrects the four months of existing offsets. One line in the Codex sanitizer.

A read helper is still worth doing — just for different reasons: it de-duplicates the `resolveTranscriptPath` + `os.ReadFile` pair that's copied three times, and it's what kills finalize's redundant full-size re-read. Those are general wins. It just shouldn't be sold as the coordinate fix.

71	func findCodexRollout(t *testing.T, codexHome string) string {

80	func readCodexSessionID(t *testing.T, rolloutPath string) string {
81		t.Helper()
82	
83		data, err := os.ReadFile(rolloutPath)
84		require.NoError(t, err)
85	
86		// Codex rollout files are JSONL; the session id lives in the payload of the
87		// first "session_meta" line. Parse line-by-line rather than anchoring a
88		// regex on field order — Codex reorders JSON keys between versions (the old
89		// regex silently stopped matching on Codex 0.142.x). This mirrors the CLI's
90		// own parser in cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/transcript.go.
91		for _, raw := range bytes.Split(data, []byte("\n")) {
92			if len(bytes.TrimSpace(raw)) == 0 {
93				continue
94			}
95			var line struct {
96				Type    string          `json:"type"`
97				Payload json.RawMessage `json:"payload"`
98			}
99			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &line); err != nil || line.Type != "session_meta" {
100				continue
101			}
102			var payload struct {
103				ID string `json:"id"`
104			}
105			require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(line.Payload, &payload))
106			require.NotEmpty(t, payload.ID, "session_meta payload missing id")
107			return payload.ID
108		}
109	
110		t.Fatalf("session_meta line not found in rollout %s", rolloutPath)
111		return ""
112	}
113	
114	// appendCompactedEncryptedHistory appends the two encrypted-payload shapes Entire
115	// has to make replayable, so a resume of the restored transcript exercises both:
116	//
117	//   - a top-level `response_item` whose payload type is `compaction`. Sanitization
118	//     strips its encrypted_content but KEEPS the line, so the stored transcript
119	//     stays line-aligned with the rollout (offsets are counted on the rollout and
120	//     applied to the stored copy). This is the shape that decides whether Codex
121	//     tolerates a compaction item with no payload.
122	//   - a `compacted` line whose replacement_history carries reasoning and compaction
123	//     items. Those nested items are removed outright — they are array elements, so
124	//     removing them cannot shift line numbers.
125	func appendCompactedEncryptedHistory(t *testing.T, rolloutPath string) {
126		t.Helper()
127	
128		lines := []map[string]any{
129			{
130				"timestamp": "2026-04-08T12:00:00.000Z",
131				"type":      "response_item",
132				"payload": map[string]any{
133					"type":              "compaction",
134					"encrypted_content": "REDACTED",
135				},
136			},
137			{
138				"timestamp": "2026-04-08T12:00:01.000Z",
139				"type":      "compacted",
140				"payload": map[string]any{
141					"message": "",
142					"replacement_history": []map[string]any{
143						{
144							"type": "message",
145							"role": "user",
146							"content": []map[string]any{
147								{"type": "input_text", "text": "hello"},
148							},
149						},
150						{
151							"type":              "reasoning",
152							"summary":           []map[string]any{{"text": "brief"}},
153							"encrypted_content": "REDACTED",
154						},
155						{
156							"type":              "compaction",
157							"encrypted_content": "REDACTED",
158						},
159					},
160				},
161			},
162		}
163	
164		f, err := os.OpenFile(rolloutPath, os.O_APPEND|os.O_WRONLY, 0)
165		require.NoError(t, err)
166		defer f.Close()
167	
168		for _, line := range lines {
169			encoded, err := json.Marshal(line)
170			require.NoError(t, err)
171			_, err = f.Write(append(encoded, '\n'))
172			require.NoError(t, err)
173		}
174	}
175	
176	// assertRestoredCompactionStripped verifies the restored rollout carries a
177	// top-level compaction item whose encrypted payload was stripped while its LINE
178	// survived. That is the shape the subsequent `codex resume` has to tolerate, and
179	// asserting it here stops the test from passing vacuously if the fixture, the
180	// sanitizer, or the restore path ever stops producing it.
181	func assertRestoredCompactionStripped(t *testing.T, rolloutPath string) {
182		t.Helper()
183	
184		data, err := os.ReadFile(rolloutPath)
185		require.NoError(t, err)
186		require.NotContains(t, string(data), "encrypted_content",
187			"restored rollout still carries encrypted payloads")
188	
189		var sawStrippedCompaction bool
190		for _, raw := range bytes.Split(data, []byte("\n")) {
191			if len(bytes.TrimSpace(raw)) == 0 {
192				continue
193			}
194			var line struct {
195				Type    string          `json:"type"`
196				Payload json.RawMessage `json:"payload"`
197			}
198			if json.Unmarshal(raw, &line) != nil || line.Type != "response_item" {
199				continue
200			}
201			var payload map[string]any
202			if json.Unmarshal(line.Payload, &payload) != nil {
203				continue
204			}
205			if payload["type"] == "compaction" {
206				sawStrippedCompaction = true
207				require.NotContains(t, payload, "encrypted_content",
208					"compaction item kept its encrypted payload")
209			}
210		}
211	
212		require.True(t, sawStrippedCompaction,
213			"restored rollout has no top-level compaction item — the test did not exercise "+
214				"the payload-less compaction shape, so its result is meaningless")
215	}

content.text:
**Option 1 works.** Codex 0.143.0 accepts a compaction item with its payload stripped.

The logged evidence — `payload keys: [type]` — is the whole answer: the restored rollout contains `{"type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"compaction"}}`, the line survives, and `codex resume` reached the prompt with no `invalid_encrypted_content`.

## Why the first green run didn't count

The first run passed, but I couldn't prove it exercised the change — the e2e fixture only had *nested* compaction items, and nesting is unaffected by this change. So I added a top-level one plus a hard coverage assertion, and the second run **failed**. That failure was my helper's fault, not the fix's, but it surfaced something real:

**`entire resume` doesn't overwrite the agent's rollout — it writes a new one.** Same session id, new timestamped filename, so the home ends up with both:

```
original: rollout-2026-08-05T13-29-32-019fd1af-…jsonl   (local time, still has encrypted_content)
restored: rollout-2026-08-05T11-29-32-019fd1af-…jsonl   (UTC, stripped)
```

`findCodexRollout` asserts exactly one rollout, which is correct pre-resume and wrong after. Worth knowing independently of this work — and note the two filenames differ by timezone, which is its own latent oddity.

## What's now verified

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Restored rollout has a top-level compaction item | ✓ `payload keys: [type]` |
| Its encrypted payload is stripped | ✓ |
| No `encrypted_content` anywhere in the restored file | ✓ |
| The `compacted` line survives | ✓ |
| `codex resume` reaches the prompt | ✓ |
| No `invalid_encrypted_content` | ✓ |

Plus, locally: `mise run fmt && lint` → 0 issues, `test:ci` → `TEST_EXIT=0`.

## The change

`sanitizeRolloutLine` now treats `compaction`/`compaction_summary` exactly like `reasoning` — strip `encrypted_content`, keep the line — rather than dropping the line. Nested items inside `replacement_history` are still removed, since array removal can't shift line numbers.

Three existing tests had to be updated because they **codified the drift as expected behavior**. The most telling is `TestUpdateCommitted_CodexCompactSanitizedLikeInitialWrite`: given `[alpha, compaction, beta, gamma]` with `CheckpointTranscriptStart: 2`, it required **`beta` to be absent** from the checkpoint slice. That absent `beta` *was* the bug, asserted as correct. It now yields `[beta, gamma]`.

One honest limit: the sanitizer strips only the `encrypted_content` key, so a future Codex version stashing ciphertext under a different key would slip through — but that's pre-existing behavior for `reasoning` items, and I kept it uniform rather than blanking to a bare `type` (which would be more robust for stripping and riskier for replay). My own integration fixture had used an invented `payload.blob` key; I corrected it to the real shape.

Nothing committed on this branch yet — `soph/codex-compaction-preserve-line-numbering`, stacked on the open PR #1901. Want me to commit and open a follow-up PR? It's worth noting there that this retroactively fixes the four months of existing checkpoint offsets, since raw and stored line counts now coincide.

input.content:
## Problem

`CheckpointTranscriptStart` marks where a checkpoint's slice of a session begins. It is **counted on the agent's raw rollout** but **applied to the stored, sanitized `full.jsonl`** — and for Codex those two files had different line counts, because `SanitizePortableTranscript` dropped `compaction` / `compaction_summary` lines outright.

So every offset into a stored Codex transcript was too large by the number of dropped lines before it. `transcript.SliceFromLine` then either starts N lines late or, when the offset exceeds the stored length, returns nothing.

```
raw rollout (counted)              stored full.jsonl (sliced)
1 session_meta                     1 session_meta
2 user "add feature"               2 user "add feature"
3 reasoning + encrypted_content    3 reasoning (key stripped)
4 compaction                       — dropped
5 assistant "done"                 4 assistant "done"

CheckpointTranscriptStart = 5, but the stored file has 4 lines.
```

**Broken since 2026-04-10** (#878, first shipped in v0.5.4) — roughly four months. #878 never touched the offsets; it added sanitization to the committed-write path and silently invalidated an invariant introduced ten weeks earlier in `faa4701f0` ("feat(explain): scope transcript and prompts to checkpoint boundaries"), which had been correct when nothing altered the stored copy.

Nothing caught it because the assumption lived in one package and was broken from another. In fact a test grew up around the symptom and asserted it as correct — see below.

### Scope

Narrower than it sounds, and no data was lost:

- **Codex only** — the only agent with a line-dropping sanitizer. Redaction, image externalization, and chunking all rewrite or split *within* line boundaries, so raw and stored counts match for every other agent.
- Only sessions containing a **top-level** `compaction`/`compaction_summary` item. Items nested in a `compacted` line's `replacement_history` are array elements — removing them cannot shift line numbers.
- Affects `entire explain --verbose` checkpoint scoping and the compact-transcript boundary. **Token accounting and growth detection are unaffected** — they apply the offset to the raw live transcript, so they were always internally consistent.

## Fix

Treat `compaction`/`compaction_summary` exactly like `reasoning`: strip `encrypted_content`, **keep the line**. Four lines of production change.

Nested items in `replacement_history` are still removed outright, since array removal can't shift line numbers.

Why this over the alternatives:

- **It repairs history.** Raw and stored line counts coincide again, so the offsets already written across four months of checkpoints become correct retroactively. Nothing else does that — the raw transcript was never stored, so a drop count can't be recovered after the fact.
- **No migration.** No basis-marker field, no version gate, no re-derivation of in-flight session watermarks.
- **No agent interface change.** The alternative of sanitizing at the read boundary would have to reach `GetTranscriptPosition` / `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` / `ExtractPrompts` — path-based capabilities implemented by 8 built-in agents *and* forwarded over the external-agent protocol, so it would be a wire-format change for third-party agents.

## Verification

The open question was whether Codex tolerates a compaction item with no payload. Answered with a real `codex resume` against Codex CLI 0.143.0:

```
restored top-level compaction item, payload keys: [type]
```

The rollout `entire resume` writes now contains `{"type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"compaction"}}`, Codex loads it, reaches the prompt, and prints no `invalid_encrypted_content`.

Two things were needed to make that test mean anything:

1. **The e2e fixture only had *nested* compaction items**, which this change doesn't affect — so it would have passed without exercising the fix. It now also appends a top-level one.
2. **A coverage assertion** (`assertRestoredCompactionStripped`) that fails if the restored rollout lacks the payload-less compaction shape. Worth having permanently: it's the difference between "green" and "green *and* covered".

## Tests that had to change

Three existing tests pinned the old drop behavior. The notable one is `TestUpdateCommitted_CodexCompactSanitizedLikeInitialWrite`: given `[alpha, compaction, beta, gamma]` with `CheckpointTranscriptStart: 2`, it required **`beta` to be absent** from the checkpoint slice. That missing `beta` *was* the bug, asserted as expected behavior. It now correctly yields `[beta, gamma]`.

`mise run fmt && mise run lint` → 0 issues. `mise run test:ci` → pass, vogon canary green.

## Notes

- The sanitizer strips only the `encrypted_content` key, so ciphertext under a different key would survive. That is pre-existing behavior for `reasoning` items and is kept uniform here rather than blanking payloads to a bare `type` — more robust for stripping, riskier for replay.
- Incidental finding: `entire resume` does **not** overwrite the agent's rollout; it writes a fresh one for the same session id under a new timestamped name, so the Codex home holds both afterwards. The test helper had to account for that.

I'll wait for CI before committing. Meanwhile, here's the plan, since making these truly independent needs one adjustment on the existing PR:

**You're right that it's a distinct PR** — only one file coupled them, and it's test-only.

| | |
|---|---|
| **PR B (new, off `main`)** | `soph/codex-keep-compaction-line` — the 4-line sanitizer fix + test updates. Applied to main cleanly; only conflict was an import block that belonged to #1901's fast-path tests. |
| **PR A (#1901)** | needs a small fixup so the two don't collide |

## Why #1901 needs a touch either way

Its `codex_shadow_sanitize_test.go` (which only exists on that branch) asserts the **old** behavior:

1. `!strings.Contains(stored, "compaction")` — expects the line dropped.
2. Its fixture puts ciphertext under an invented `payload.blob` key. Since the sanitizer only strips `encrypted_content`, that ciphertext would survive once PR B lands and the "ciphertext gone" assertion would fail.
3. Its ordering test relies on a top-level compaction line being *dropped* to orphan an asset — a scenario PR B removes.

So whichever merges second breaks the other. The fix is three edits to that one file, all defensible on their own merits: use the **real** `encrypted_content` key (the fixture was simply wrong — real Codex uses it), scope the assertion to intent (ciphertext and the key are gone) rather than to drop-vs-strip, and retarget the ordering test at the nested-history case, which is the one place sanitization still discards content.

After that, either PR can merge first. I already have all three edits written — they're in the stash from the earlier stacked attempt.

Once CI comes back I'll commit B, push, open the PR, then push the compatibility commit to #1901.

I'll hold here until the suite reports. To confirm the plan we've converged on:

**One PR (#1901), three commits** — each internally consistent so the history still bisects:

| Commit | Fix |
|---|---|
| `79ef6b8d3` | Shadow-branch sanitization + the `TranscriptSanitizer` capability + growth-baseline coordinate fix |
| `35f194faf` | Sanitize before externalize/redact (condensation + finalize) |
| *new* | Keep compaction lines so stored transcripts stay line-aligned |

This drops the compatibility fixup entirely — the `codex_shadow_sanitize_test.go` edits land in the third commit alongside the change that requires them, rather than needing to be back-ported to keep two PRs from breaking each other.

The one tradeoff worth naming: the PR now mixes a perf/ordering fix with a **behavioral** change to Codex replay (the payload-less compaction item, validated by the paid e2e). If that ever needs backing out because Codex tightens its deserializer, it's a single-commit revert rather than a single-PR revert — which is why I'm keeping it as its own commit rather than squashing it in.

The isolated CI run currently finishing is still useful either way: it validates the sanitizer change against plain `main`, independent of the other two commits, which is evidence I wouldn't get once it's stacked.

Then: commit, re-run the full suite on the stacked branch, update the PR title and description to cover all three fixes, and push.

CheckpointTranscriptStart marks where a checkpoint's slice of a session
begins. It is counted on the agent's raw rollout but applied to the stored,
sanitized full.jsonl — and for Codex those two files had different line counts,
because SanitizePortableTranscript dropped compaction/compaction_summary lines
outright. Every offset into a stored Codex transcript was therefore too large by
the number of dropped lines before it, so SliceFromLine either started N lines
late or, once the offset exceeded the stored length, returned nothing.

Broken since 2026-04-10 (#878, shipped in v0.5.4) — about four months. #878 never
touched the offsets; it added sanitization to the committed-write path and
silently invalidated an invariant introduced ten weeks earlier in faa4701f0
("feat(explain): scope transcript and prompts to checkpoint boundaries"), which
was correct while nothing altered the stored copy. The assumption lived in one
package and was broken from another, so nothing caught it.

Fix: treat compaction/compaction_summary exactly like reasoning — strip
encrypted_content, keep the line. Items nested in a compacted line's
replacement_history are still removed outright, since array removal cannot shift
line numbers.

This repairs history rather than just stopping the bleeding: raw and stored line
counts coincide again, so the offsets already written across four months of
checkpoints become correct retroactively. No basis-marker field, no migration of
in-flight session watermarks, and no agent interface change (sanitizing at the
read boundary would have to reach GetTranscriptPosition /
ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset / ExtractPrompts, which are path-based and
forwarded over the external-agent protocol).

line-dropping sanitizer), only sessions with a top-level compaction item, and
only `explain --verbose` scoping plus the compact-transcript boundary. Token
accounting and growth detection apply the offset to the raw live transcript, so
they were always internally consistent.

rollout carries {"type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"compaction"}}, Codex
loads it, reaches the prompt, and prints no invalid_encrypted_content. Two fixes

input.content:
Three related fixes to Entire's Codex transcript-storage pipeline, kept as separate commits.

## Problem 1 — sanitization ran last, or not at all

Codex rollouts carry state that cannot be replayed out of a checkpoint: encrypted reasoning payloads and compaction blobs, bound to the originating session. `codex.SanitizePortableTranscript` strips them, but it ran **last**, and on one path never:

- The Stop path wrote the **raw** rollout to `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl`, and the generic metadata-dir walker redacted every blob without ever sanitizing.
- Condensation and the Stop finalize rewrite externalized images and redacted the **raw** transcript; the store sanitized only afterwards, on the way into the tree.

Base64 ciphertext is the pathological input for redaction's entropy layer (`secretPattern` + Shannon ≥ 4.5), so the 8 layers scanned megabytes that sanitization then discarded. On a synthetic 27.4 MB rollout, **redaction alone took 47 s** (0.26 MB/s). That is the timeout; raising the timeout only hides it.

The ordering was also wrong in a second way: image externalization walks every string leaf, so an image inside content that sanitization later discards was lifted into an asset blob + manifest entry whose referencing transcript line then vanished — an orphaned asset, stored and pushed for the life of the checkpoint.

## Problem 2 — stored transcripts were not line-aligned with the rollout

`CheckpointTranscriptStart` marks where a checkpoint's slice begins. It is **counted on the raw rollout** but **applied to the stored, sanitized `full.jsonl`** — and those had different line counts, because sanitization dropped `compaction` / `compaction_summary` lines outright.

```
raw rollout (counted)              stored full.jsonl (sliced)
1 session_meta                     1 session_meta
2 user "add feature"               2 user "add feature"
3 reasoning + encrypted_content    3 reasoning (key stripped)
4 compaction                       — dropped
5 assistant "done"                 4 assistant "done"

CheckpointTranscriptStart = 5, but the stored file has 4 lines.
```

**Broken since 2026-04-10** (#878, shipped in v0.5.4) — about four months. #878 never touched the offsets; it added sanitization to the committed-write path and silently invalidated an invariant introduced ten weeks earlier in `faa4701f0` ("feat(explain): scope transcript and prompts to checkpoint boundaries"), which was correct while nothing altered the stored copy. The assumption lived in one package and was broken from another.

No data was lost, and the scope is narrow: **Codex only** (the only agent with a line-dropping sanitizer — redaction, externalization, and chunking all stay within line boundaries), only sessions with a **top-level** compaction item, and only `explain --verbose` scoping plus the compact-transcript boundary. Token accounting and growth detection apply the offset to the raw live transcript, so they were always internally consistent.

## The three commits

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| `79ef6b8d3` | New optional `agent.TranscriptSanitizer` capability, applied at the Stop path where Entire takes custody of its copy. Codex implements it; the agent's own rollout is never modified. |
| `35f194faf` | Sanitize **before** externalize and redact, in both condensation and the Stop finalize rewrite. |
| `9e5af6211` | Keep compaction lines (strip the payload, don't drop the line) so stored transcripts stay line-aligned. |

Every path that builds a stored transcript now runs **sanitize → externalize images → redact**:

| Path | Where |
|---|---|
| Stop / shadow branch | `lifecycle.go`, before `full.jsonl` is written |
| Post-commit condensation | `prepareTranscriptForStorage` in `manual_commit_condensation.go` |
| Stop finalize (full-session rewrite) | `manual_commit_hooks.go` |
| Safety net for callers with no live agent (`entire import`) | `checkpoint.sanitizeForAgentType` |

## Results

Same 27.4 MB rollout, end to end through the real Codex hooks:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Stop hook | (47 s in redaction alone) | **456 ms** |
| Commit / condense | (same scan again) | **506 ms** |
| Stored shadow blob | 27.4 MB | **87 KB** (0.32%) |

And the line-alignment fix **repairs history**: raw and stored line counts coincide again, so offsets already written across four months of checkpoints become correct retroactively. Nothing else achieves that — the raw transcript was never stored, so a drop count cannot be recovered after the fact. It also needs no basis-marker field, no migration of in-flight session watermarks, and no agent interface change (sanitizing at the read boundary would have to reach `GetTranscriptPosition` / `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` / `ExtractPrompts`, which are path-based and forwarded over the external-agent protocol — a wire-format change for third-party agents).

## Things reviewers should know

**The growth baseline had to move with the shadow blob.** `SessionState.CheckpointTranscriptSize` is compared against the shadow transcript blob's size in `sessionHasNewContent`. Shrinking that blob ~99% while leaving the baseline measured on the raw transcript makes `blobSize > baseline` false *forever* — the session silently stops condensing after its first commit. `CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline` keeps both sides in the sanitized coordinate, with a regression test. The codebase already carried a warning about this trap from when image externalization hit it.

**The store dispatches on agent type explicitly, on purpose.** An earlier iteration resolved the agent via `agent.GetByAgentType`, which reads cleaner. It is unsafe here: the registry is populated by package `init`, so the lookup only succeeds when something else in the binary happens to import `agent/codex`. When it doesn't, sanitization silently degrades to a no-op — reintroducing the bug with no signal. The comment says so, so nobody "cleans it up" again.

**Sanitization has a fast path.** A marker pre-scan plus a change flag means an already-sanitized transcript returns its original backing array instead of a deep JSON parse and two full-size copies (167 ms → 628 µs). That is what makes calling it from every storage path affordable.

**Two call sites needed the ordering fix, not one.** `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` rebuilds the stored transcript independently of `CondenseSession`, so fixing condensation alone left the bug live in the finalize path.

## Verification

The open question for the line-alignment fix was whether Codex tolerates a compaction item with no payload. Answered with a real `codex resume` against Codex CLI 0.143.0:

```
restored top-level compaction item, payload keys: [type]
```

Codex loads it, reaches the prompt, prints no `invalid_encrypted_content`. Two things were needed to make that test mean anything: the e2e fixture only had **nested** compaction items (unaffected by this change, so it would have passed without exercising it), and it now asserts the restored rollout actually contains the payload-less shape rather than trusting a green run.

New tests:

- `TestCodexShadowBranch_SanitizesTranscript` — the shadow blob has no ciphertext, keeps the conversation, and stays line-aligned with the rollout.
- `TestCodexShadowBranch_GrowthStillDetectedAfterCommit` — a second commit still condenses (the coordinate-coupling guard).
- `TestCodexCondense_NoAssetsFromSanitizedAwayContent` — no asset is externalized out of content sanitization discards.
- `TestSanitizePortableTranscript_PreservesLineNumbering` — line-for-line alignment across every transform.
- `TestSanitizePortableTranscript_{UnchangedInputReturnsSameBytes,IdempotentBytes}` — the fast path and byte-idempotency.
- 7 unit tests on the capability contract (idempotency, passthrough, nil agent, fail-safe on a nil return).

Three existing tests pinned the old drop behavior. The telling one is `TestUpdateCommitted_CodexCompactSanitizedLikeInitialWrite`: given `[alpha, compaction, beta, gamma]` with `CheckpointTranscriptStart: 2`, it required **`beta` to be absent** from the checkpoint slice. That missing `beta` *was* the bug, asserted as expected behavior; it now correctly yields `[beta, gamma]`.

`mise run fmt && mise run lint` → 0 issues. `mise run test:ci` → pass, vogon canary green. Each commit verified to build and pass standalone, so the history bisects.

## Notes and deliberate omissions

- The sanitizer strips only the `encrypted_content` key, so ciphertext under a different key would survive. That is pre-existing behavior for `reasoning` items, kept uniform rather than blanking payloads to a bare `type` — more robust for stripping, riskier for replay.
- Incidental finding: `entire resume` does **not** overwrite the agent's rollout; it writes a fresh one for the same session id under a new timestamped name, so the Codex home holds both afterwards.
- **Not in scope:** finalize still re-reads the live rollout and sanitizes it again (one genuinely full-size redundant pass per Stop — fixing it means threading the sanitized bytes through the turn-end chain); and the read-side chokepoint (`readLiveTranscript` / `ReadTranscriptForStorage`) that would de-duplicate the resolve+read pair copied three times.

content.text:
Done. **[PR #1901](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1901)** — one PR, three commits, 18 files, +1008/−112. Tree clean, branch in sync with origin, scratch branches removed.

| Commit | Fix |
|---|---|
| `79ef6b8d3` | Shadow-branch sanitization + `TranscriptSanitizer` capability + growth-baseline coordinate fix |
| `35f194faf` | Sanitize before externalize/redact (condensation **and** finalize) |
| `9e5af6211` | Keep compaction lines so stored transcripts stay line-aligned |

Retitled to *"sanitize Codex transcripts before redaction and keep them line-aligned"* since it now covers both problems, and the body leads with the two user-visible symptoms — 47 s → ~500 ms per hook, and four months of misaligned transcript offsets.

## On the structure question

Folding was the right call, and it removed real work rather than just moving it. The two PRs would have broken each other in a way neither description would have revealed: #1901's new integration test asserted `!contains(stored, "compaction")` and used an invented `payload.blob` fixture key, both of which the line-alignment fix invalidates. Whichever merged second would have gone red. Keeping the third change as its own commit preserves what mattered from the split — it's independently revertable if Codex ever tightens its deserializer, which is the one piece here validated by external behavior rather than by our own tests.

## Worth flagging on the way out

**The four-month bug was found by asking "why?" about something I'd accepted as given.** I'd been treating "compaction lines get dropped" as a fixed constraint and building offset-translation machinery around it. Your question turned it into a one-line fix that repairs existing checkpoints instead of adding a migration.

**A test had encoded the bug as correct.** `TestUpdateCommitted_CodexCompactSanitizedLikeInitialWrite` required `beta` to be *absent* from a checkpoint slice — that absence was the data loss, asserted as expected behavior. Worth remembering when a test seems to justify surprising behavior.

**The first e2e pass was worthless.** The fixture only had nested compaction items, which this change doesn't touch. Adding a coverage assertion made it fail, which is how I learned `entire resume` writes a *new* rollout rather than overwriting. The assertion is now permanent so it can't pass vacuously again.

**Two CI results were misleading.** One reported success because I piped through `tail` and read `tail`'s exit code; another failed on the known subprocess segfault flake plus a 9-minute hang in a pre-push test that then passed in 0.00s. Both verified rather than assumed — worth avoiding `| tail` on `test:ci`.

Still deferred and noted in the PR: finalize's redundant full-size re-read, the read-side chokepoint, and the shadow-branch → single-ref work (step 2 from earlier).

## Pull request overview

This PR introduces an agent-level transcript sanitization capability and ensures Entire sanitizes stored transcript copies **before** downstream processing (image externalization and redaction), preventing non-portable Codex state from being persisted and avoiding expensive redaction scans over ciphertext-heavy payloads.

In writeTranscript's TranscriptPath fallback, the transcript is redacted before being sanitized. That reintroduces the original performance/correctness problem for callers that reach the store via TranscriptPath (e.g. import): the redaction scan still processes ciphertext that sanitization would later discard, and the stored-copy pipeline order no longer matches sanitize → … → redact. Sanitizing the raw bytes before calling redact.JSONLBytes keeps the intended ordering while still ensuring untrusted disk content is redacted before storage.

As written, this can mislead future changes (e.g. assuming images are preserved in shadow transcripts). Consider documenting the shadow-branch behavior separately and limiting the 3-step pipeline claim to the committed-checkpoint/finalize paths where image externalization actually runs.

content.content:
**Transcript sanitization (before redaction).** Entire never modifies the agent's
own transcript, but the copy it stores goes through the agent's optional
`agent.TranscriptSanitizer` first, at the point Entire takes custody (the Stop path
in `lifecycle.go`, before `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` is written). Codex
implements it to strip encrypted reasoning payloads and compaction blobs, which are
bound to the originating session and cannot be replayed out of a checkpoint.

Every path that builds a stored transcript runs the same three steps in the same
order — **sanitize → externalize images → redact**:

| Path | Where |
|---|---|
| Stop (shadow branch) | `lifecycle.go`, before `full.jsonl` is written |
| Post-commit condensation | `prepareTranscriptForStorage` in `manual_commit_condensation.go` |
| Stop finalize (full-session rewrite) | `manual_commit_hooks.go`, before `extractSessionImages` |

Each step must precede the next. Sanitizing first avoids externalizing images out of
items that are about to be discarded — that would store an asset whose referencing
transcript line disappears moments later — and avoids redacting megabytes of
ciphertext only to throw it away; base64 is the pathological input for the entropy
layer, so a large Codex rollout otherwise costs tens of seconds per Stop *and* per
commit. Externalizing before redaction is required because base64 is high-entropy
and redaction would otherwise flag and destroy it.

The sanitize transform is idempotent, so a downstream write path can call it without
knowing whether an upstream path already did (`checkpoint.sanitizeForAgentType` is
the store's own belt-and-braces call).

One coupling to respect when changing this: `SessionState.CheckpointTranscriptSize`
is a growth baseline compared against the shadow transcript blob's size in

content.text:
Copilot left one review with **2 inline comments**. Both were legitimate; I've addressed both, with one correction to its reasoning.

## 1. `persistent.go` — redact-before-sanitize in the `TranscriptPath` fallback

**Valid, fixed.** That block did redact raw bytes before sanitizing, contradicting the pipeline order everywhere else. Now sanitizes first.

Two corrections to the comment though:

- **It's not a correctness problem.** Copilot said "performance/correctness". I tested this: reverting the fix, my new test still passes. The trailing `sanitizeForAgentType` call already guaranteed the stored bytes were sanitized, and redaction is JSON-aware, so redact-then-sanitize still ends with `encrypted_content` deleted. The two orders are **indistinguishable by output** — only the wasted redaction scan was real.
- **Its example is wrong.** It cited `import` as reaching this path. `agentimport` passes in-memory `Transcript` (`RedactedBytes`); I re-verified that **no production caller** sets the store's `WriteOptions.TranscriptPath`. The two `TranscriptPath:` hits in production are `StepContext` (shadow path) and `SessionState` — different structs.

So it's a latent trap on an unreachable path rather than a live bug. Still worth fixing: it contradicts the documented invariant, and it's two lines.

I added `TestWriteCommitted_CodexSanitizesTranscriptFromPath` — that fallback had **zero** tests before, which is why the ordering drifted there unnoticed. I checked it's not a vacuous ordering test and said so in the comment, rather than letting it imply coverage it doesn't have.

## 2. Docs overstate the shadow-branch pipeline

**Valid, and my error.** I wrote that *every* path runs sanitize → externalize → redact. Verified: `extractSessionImages` is called only from condensation and finalize — **never** on the Stop/shadow path, which is sanitize → redact.

That mattered more than a wording nit, and Copilot named the exact consequence: someone would assume shadow transcripts preserve images. They don't — inline base64 in a shadow transcript gets destroyed by redaction, since externalization (which exists precisely to protect it) doesn't run there. Fixed in both `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, with a per-path pipeline table and an explicit note that assets exist only under committed checkpoints.

## Status

`mise run lint` → 0 issues; affected packages green; full `test:ci` running. Note Copilot reviewed **15 of 18 files** — its review predates the third commit, so the line-alignment change hasn't been reviewed yet.

I'll push the review fixes as a fourth commit once CI confirms, and reply to both threads — including the correction that the first one isn't a correctness issue, since leaving that unchallenged would misrepresent the change to anyone reading the thread.

Waiting on a clean run. Summary of the review response so far:

## Both Copilot comments were valid; both fixed

**`persistent.go` — redact before sanitize in the `TranscriptPath` fallback.** Fixed to sanitize first. But two corrections to its reasoning, which I'll post on the thread rather than accept silently:

- **Not a correctness issue.** I tested it: reverting my fix, the new test still passes. The trailing `sanitizeForAgentType` already guaranteed sanitized stored bytes, and redaction is JSON-aware, so both orders end with `encrypted_content` deleted. Only the wasted redaction scan was real.
- **Its example is wrong.** `import` doesn't reach that path — `agentimport` passes in-memory `RedactedBytes`. No production caller sets the store's `WriteOptions.TranscriptPath` at all.

Still worth fixing as a latent trap, and I added the first-ever test for that fallback — with a comment stating plainly that it does *not* pin the ordering, so it can't be mistaken for coverage it lacks.

**Docs overstated the shadow-branch pipeline.** My error. `extractSessionImages` runs only in condensation and finalize — never on the Stop/shadow path. Copilot also named the real consequence: someone would assume shadow transcripts preserve images, and they don't (inline base64 there gets destroyed by redaction, since externalization doesn't run). Corrected in both `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` and `CLAUDE.md` with a per-path table.

## About those CI failures

Two `test:ci` runs failed with timeouts and I was about to call them flakes — but the second failure made it a pattern, so I dug in. **A concurrent e2e canary run from a different checkout (`cli_experiments_2`) was saturating the machine** (load 17.6). Different tests hung each run, all simultaneously at ~9m40s, all spawning subprocesses; each passes in ~3s in isolation.

Worth flagging for your own runs: parallel test suites across checkouts on this box will produce phantom integration timeouts.

Once the clean run confirms, I'll push the review fixes as a fourth commit and reply to both threads. Also noting on the PR that Copilot reviewed 15 of 18 files — the line-alignment commit arrived after its review, so that part is still unreviewed.

fix(checkpoint): sanitize before redacting in the TranscriptPath fallback

Review follow-up. Two issues from Copilot's review of #1901, both real.

1. writeTranscript's TranscriptPath fallback redacted raw bytes before sanitizing,
   contradicting the sanitize-before-redact order every other path follows. It is
   the one way raw bytes reach the store, so it is also the one place where the
   wasted work is real: redaction scanning ciphertext that sanitization discards
   moments later.

   Note this was NOT a content-correctness problem, contrary to the review comment:
   the trailing sanitizeForAgentType call already guaranteed the stored bytes were
   sanitized, and redaction is JSON-aware, so redact-then-sanitize still ended with
   encrypted_content deleted. The two orders are indistinguishable by output. Fixed
   anyway — it is a latent trap that contradicts the documented invariant.

   Also adds the first test for that fallback, which previously had none (which is
   how the ordering drifted there unnoticed). The test asserts the stored result and
   says explicitly that it does not pin the ordering, so it cannot be mistaken for
   coverage it does not provide.

2. The docs claimed every storage path runs sanitize -> externalize -> redact. That
   is wrong for the Stop/shadow path: extractSessionImages is only called from
   condensation and finalize, so the shadow copy is sanitize -> redact. The
   consequence is worth stating rather than glossing — inline images in a shadow
   transcript are subject to redaction, because the externalization step that exists
   to protect high-entropy base64 does not run there, and assets/manifest.json
   exists only under committed checkpoints. Corrected in both the architecture doc
   and CLAUDE.md with a per-path pipeline table.

16	`//go:norace`. `syscall.forkAndExecInChild` is `//go:norace` and justified calling rawSyscall
17	because "they are assembly functions" — true on darwin until 1.26. So under `-race` the fork
18	child ran TSan instrumentation and faulted in `__tsan::TraceSwitchPartImpl` (null ThreadState
19	field deref, SIGSEGV at `0x8`). Upstream: golang/go#79804, CL 786620, 1.26 backport #79806.
20	
21	**The fix, verifiable locally:**
22	`diff ~/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.{4,5}/src/syscall/syscall_darwin.go`
23	→ 1.26.5 adds `//go:norace` to `rawSyscall`, `rawSyscall6`, `rawSyscall9`, `errno`, `errnoX`,
24	`errnoPtr`, and corrects the `exec_libc2.go` comment. **So: bump the Go pin (mise.toml +
25	go.mod) rather than disabling `-race`.** Affected range is go1.26.0–1.26.4 only.
26	
27	**Diagnostics that worked** (reuse for any "spawned subprocess segfaulted" report):
28	`~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/<binary>-*.ips` — look for
29	`asi: ["crashed on child side of fork pre-exec"]`, `threadCount: 1`, `procName == parentProc`.

32	repo-code changes**, so std frames symbolize reliably even from a non-matching build — but
33	repo-code frames resolve to visible nonsense, so never trust those without a UUID match.
34	`go tool objdump` the suspect function to confirm instrumentation is really present.

37	- Did not `diff` the newer Go already installed on disk, nor search upstream for the `.ips`
38	  annotation string. Both would have found the shipped fix in one step, before writing a
39	  duplicate bug report.

---
name: integration-subprocess-segfault-flake
description: "Intermittent SIGSEGV from spawned subprocesses under -race on darwin was a Go bug fixed in go1.26.5 (rawSyscall missing //go:norace). Fix = bump the Go pin, not a test workaround."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 540681cb-37a8-48d9-b289-533d545fbe66
  modified: 2026-08-05T12:20:33.396Z
---

Under `-race` on **darwin**, a Go test that forks could die with `signal: segmentation fault` in
the child before `exec`. **Go toolchain bug, FIXED IN go1.26.5** (released 2026-07-01).

**Root cause.** Go 1.26 turned darwin's `syscall.rawSyscall` from a bodiless
runtime/assembly declaration into a real Go function (`rawsyscalln` refactor) without adding
`//go:norace`. `syscall.forkAndExecInChild` is `//go:norace` and justified calling rawSyscall
because "they are assembly functions" — true on darwin until 1.26. So under `-race` the fork
child ran TSan instrumentation and faulted in `__tsan::TraceSwitchPartImpl` (null ThreadState
field deref, SIGSEGV at `0x8`). Upstream: golang/go#79804, CL 786620, 1.26 backport #79806.

**The fix, verifiable locally:**
`diff ~/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.{4,5}/src/syscall/syscall_darwin.go`
→ 1.26.5 adds `//go:norace` to `rawSyscall`, `rawSyscall6`, `rawSyscall9`, `errno`, `errnoX`,
`errnoPtr`, and corrects the `exec_libc2.go` comment. **So: bump the Go pin (mise.toml +
go.mod) rather than disabling `-race`.** Affected range is go1.26.0–1.26.4 only.

**Diagnostics that worked** (reuse for any "spawned subprocess segfaulted" report):
`~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/<binary>-*.ips` — look for
`asi: ["crashed on child side of fork pre-exec"]`, `threadCount: 1`, `procName == parentProc`.
Symbolize `imageOffset` + `0x100000000` against a rebuild. **Go test binaries here are
bit-reproducible** (same commit → same LC_UUID) and **std-lib symbol addresses are invariant to
repo-code changes**, so std frames symbolize reliably even from a non-matching build — but
repo-code frames resolve to visible nonsense, so never trust those without a UUID match.
`go tool objdump` the suspect function to confirm instrumentation is really present.

**Mistakes made diagnosing it — don't repeat:**
- Did not `diff` the newer Go already installed on disk, nor search upstream for the `.ips`
  annotation string. Both would have found the shipped fix in one step, before writing a
  duplicate bug report.
- Claimed "the frame chain reads coherently, so the mapping must be right". Unsound — near-miss
  builds yield plausible-but-wrong chains. Establish build determinism and std-layout
  invariance instead.
- Paired a crash report to a test run without checking `procLaunch`/`captureTime` against the
  log's mtime, and wrongly concluded crashes were "often silent" (they were 17 min apart).
  Zero silent instances were ever demonstrated.
- Quoted a "~1 in 3" rate from a handful of runs; measured later as 0/8 (single package) and
  1/4 (`./...`), n far too small for the mechanism claims built on it.
- Missed one of four crash reports present in the same directory.

`.ips` retention here is only ~4 days and `Retired/` is empty, so absence of old reports proves
nothing. ReportCrash also throttles duplicates — a reproduced crash produced no new `.ips`.

Distinct from [[go-git-reconcile-flake]] (go-git "object not found", not a segfault).
See also [[git-stash-untracked-pitfall]].

content.text:
Verified. Both PR threads answered, review fixes pushed as `bd574bfbd`.

## Review response

| Comment | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `persistent.go` redact-before-sanitize | Fixed — plus two corrections posted: it wasn't a *correctness* issue (the trailing sanitize already guaranteed the content, and both orders are indistinguishable by output — I confirmed by reverting), and `import` doesn't reach that path |
| Docs overstate the shadow pipeline | Fixed — my error. `extractSessionImages` only runs in condensation/finalize, so the shadow path is `sanitize → redact`. Per-path table now, plus the sharper consequence: inline base64 there is *destroyed* by redaction, since externalization is what protects it |

Added the first-ever test for that fallback, with a comment saying plainly it does **not** pin the ordering — so it can't be mistaken for coverage it lacks.

## The CI flake has a known fix

This is the more useful outcome. Chasing the `ThreadSanitizer: CHECK failed (tsan_rtl.cpp:94)` crash led to a memory note saying it's a **Go toolchain bug fixed in go1.26.5** — and its own recorded lesson was "you failed to diff the newer Go already on disk." So I did:

```
diff go/1.26.{4,5}/src/syscall/syscall_darwin.go
→ 1.26.5 adds //go:norace to rawSyscall/rawSyscall6/rawSyscall9
```

Under `-race` on darwin, forked children ran TSan instrumentation and died pre-`exec`. Affected range is **1.26.0–1.26.4**. We pin **1.26.4** in both `go.mod` and `mise.toml`, and **1.26.5 is already installed locally**.

So the subprocess crashes polluting local runs (and plausibly CI) are a one-line pin bump, not something to keep re-verifying. I haven't made that change — it touches every build and belongs in its own PR, not one about transcript sanitization. Worth doing though; it's cheap and removes a recurring source of false red.

One correction: I earlier repeated a "~1 in 3 runs" figure for this flake. That number is unmeasured — the memory itself flags it as extrapolated from too few samples. I shouldn't have restated it.

## Status

- 4 commits, pushed, tree clean, in sync with origin
- `lint` → 0 issues; all affected packages green; the flaked tests verified 3× green in isolation
- Three phantom CI failures this round, all environmental and documented on the PR: two timeouts from a concurrent canary run in `cli_experiments_2` (load 17.6), one TSan crash
- Flagged on the PR that the bot reviewed **15 of 18 files** — the line-alignment commit, the highest-risk one, is still unreviewed

content.text:
Rebased and pushed. **[PR #1901](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1901)** — 4 commits on top of current main, 18 files, +1066/−113, **0 commits behind**, `MERGEABLE`.

## The Go bump does fix the flake

That was the real payoff. I stress-ran the test that had crashed with `ThreadSanitizer: CHECK failed` — **8× under `-race`, all green**, and the full `test:ci` came back `TEST_EXIT=0` with zero failures and no TSan crashes. Previously that suite failed 2 of 4 runs on 1.26.4.

So the subprocess crashes I'd been re-verifying all session are genuinely gone, not just quiet. Anything with that signature from here on is worth treating as a real failure rather than assumed flake.

## Rebase notes

Main had moved 8 commits with **zero file overlap** with mine, so the rebase was clean. One I watched deliberately: `408435dab` "Make git-refs the sole enable default; drop backend picker" — a checkpoint-backend change that could plausibly have broken my integration tests, since they read shadow branches and the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch directly. Ran those specifically after rebasing; all green. Worth noting CI now exercises both `test-canary (git-branch)` and `(git-refs)`.

Force-pushed with `--force-with-lease` since the rebase rewrote all four commits.

## Current state

GitHub CI is running (10 checks pending). `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` is just `REVIEW_REQUIRED` — needs a human approval, not a problem with the branch.

Two things outstanding for a reviewer, both already flagged on the PR:

- The bot review covered **15 of 18 files** and predates `4f25878fc` (keep compaction lines) — the highest-risk commit, since it's validated by an external contract (`codex resume` accepting a payload-less compaction item) rather than only our tests.
- Deferred follow-ups: finalize's redundant full-size re-read, the read-side chokepoint, and the shadow-branch → single-ref work.

One open medium finding (`019fd280-0be`, confidence 0.70) at `persistent.go:1079`:

> For `entire import` (`agentimport.go`), the transcript is redacted via `redact.JSONLBytes(full)` on the **raw** rollout before ever being sanitized… it contradicts the new CLAUDE.md claim that "every path that builds a stored transcript sanitizes before redacting."

Verified: `agentimport.go` redacts raw bytes, and there **is** a registered Codex importer. So importing Codex history paid exactly the ciphertext-scan cost this PR exists to remove. And it caught my own documentation writing a cheque the code didn't honour — I'd even told Copilot "`entire import`, which writes raw third-party rollouts" while leaving the ordering unfixed there.

Fixed by exporting `checkpoint.SanitizeTranscriptForAgentType` (one compile-time-safe implementation, no registry lookup) and calling it in `Run()` before its redaction pass.

## What the finding didn't say, and matters more

The Codex importer derives `CheckpointTranscriptStart` from **raw line indices** (`splitLineTurns`). So **`entire import` was a fourth casualty of the four-month line-offset bug** — every imported Codex turn after a compaction line would have been mis-scoped. I'd only identified `explain --verbose` and the compact boundary earlier; I missed this path entirely.

Commit 3 already fixes it, and there's a sharper consequence: had I applied this import fix *without* commit 3, sanitizing earlier in `Run()` would have **introduced** the drift into import rather than avoiding it. The two changes are load-bearing for each other, which is a point in favour of them being one PR.

Added `TestRun_CodexImportSanitizesAndKeepsOffsetsAligned` covering both properties — import had no test for either.

## Honest limit on both my review-fix tests

I checked by reverting each fix: **both tests still pass.** The store's safety-net sanitize means the stored content is identical either way, so neither the `persistent.go` fallback nor the import ordering is observable from the result. Both fixes are wasted-work fixes, not content fixes, and I've said so in both test comments rather than letting them imply coverage they don't have.
